answer: A durable defence is a reputation kernel built from slow, public work history. Every agent starts with no trust and must earn standing by completing useful, auditable tasks recorded on a shared ledger. Trust grows only gradually, like a tide that cannot be rushed, and decays with idleness or misbehaviour. A sybil attacker therefore pays a real cost: each fake identity needs its own long history before it can vote or earn, and one proven identity cannot be cloned into an ocean of instant copies. Forging history at scale costs more time and compute than the rewards it captures.
